item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate B follows the frozen contract directly and with disciplined scope; Candidate A introduces explicitly prohibited global retry/body-buffering changes and duplicates FilesService.Add logic.","reasons":["B implements the exact Upload signature, validates inputs, uses multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), and delegates directly to s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), preserving established option, request, decoding, and error behavior.","B’s tests cover multipart field name, filename, content, replay of content originating from a non-seekable io.MultiReader after a 429, validation without a request, and source-reader failure.","A does not route Upload through FilesService.Add. It duplicates Add’s option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error path, directly violating the contract and creating future drift risk.","A changes RawClient.Do to buffer nearly every io.Reader across the SDK and changes Files.Add/Update retry and streaming behavior. The contract explicitly says to preserve Add behavior and avoid refactoring unrelated request/retry machinery."],"risks_a":["Global buffering may introduce unexpected memory use and eager source-reader errors for unrelated SDK requests.","Upload’s duplicated Add implementation can diverge from Add’s API and error semantics over time.","Documentation advertises new Add/Update retry and buffering semantics outside the authorized scope."],"risks_b":["The retry test validates multipart content only on the retried request, not explicitly on both attempts.","The new tests do not explicitly verify FilesOption forwarding, although delegation to the existing Add method makes preservation straightforward."]}
